title: Per-Window Toolbar Strip
description:
Every window receives its own toolbar strip on the bottom (same as footer but floating and glassy like window options). Tools are now on window level. In the footer should only remain app mode wide commands.

Implementation: add a `toolbar` slot to `Window`/`WindowConfig` in ui/js/react/index.tsx, styled as a full-width floating glass strip at the bottom of the window body (windowOptions glass tier, no rounded corners), foldable with the same chrome pattern as WindowMeasuresChrome/WindowEngagementChrome, folded chip anchored bottom-left. Rewire framework/renderer/react/os-shell.tsx to source tools per window kind (toolNodesByKind via plugin.tools called per windowKindId) instead of one global activeToolNodes, pass each window its own ToolTree via the new toolbar slot, and strip the ToolTree/tools out of footerToolbar so the footer only keeps the app label item and the app-wide SyncAttachCard/sync tools. Update ui/styling/js/ui.css with a matching glass rule for the new data-slot, and extend Window.stories.tsx / Footer.stories.tsx and the existing test suites (framework/renderer/react/index.test.ts, in-source Window tests) accordingly. No rounded corners anywhere in the new/touched classes per repo design rule.
summary:
Fixed toolbar/command rails to expand horizontally (rightward) instead of vertically (downward) when unfolded, per dev feedback that unfolding was stacking content below the toggle and changing the window panel's effective height.

Both `window-toolbar` and `window-engagement-zone` stacks now use `flex-row items-stretch` (was `flex-col`, inherited from `windowMeasuresStackClass`) so the fold/unfold toggle sits beside its content instead of above it — the row stays a single fixed height (`h-medium`) whether folded or unfolded. Added `windowRailChromeAsideClass` (`windowMeasuresChromeClass` with `border-b-0 border-r w-auto shrink-0`) for the expanded/unfolded toggle button so its divider border is on the right (toward the content) instead of the bottom (which only made sense for vertical stacking) — the folded-chip state is unchanged (no divider needed, single button alone).

Toolbar's stack width is now always `w-fit` (hug the tool row's actual width, up to `max-w-full`) regardless of fold state, and the previous `windowToolbarOverlayFoldedClass` 14rem cap was dropped from the overlay entirely — tools can now expand as wide as the window body allows rather than being artificially capped, satisfying "tools should expand to the right." Command's overlay-level width capping (`engagementZoneSizeStyle`, min(28rem,100%)) is unchanged since that's still needed to bound the input field's width once expanded — only the internal stack direction changed, so the input now renders immediately to the right of the toggle instead of on a row below it.

Extended two tests to lock in the new DOM structure (chrome and body as row siblings, `flex-row` class, right-border divider) and fixed one stale assertion that still expected `flex-col`. Verified via the full ui-react vitest suite (199/208 passing, same 9 pre-existing unrelated tree-helper failures), framework-renderer-react (69/69), and a clean lint run.
